newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rate cut talk to drive S.African shares next week.
newsitem.headline: Rate cut talk to drive S.African shares next week.

text.p: South African shares are expected to maintain their upward trend albeit at a slower pace next week as the market searched for fresh clues on rate cut prospects, dealers and analysts said on Friday.
The market would also to take its cue from gold, which continued to grapple with support at between $328-$330 in London this week.

James Scott, an equity marketing manager at stockbroking firm Societe Generale Frankel Pollak, said the market could see some consolidation following its recent gains, adding that a lack of fresh economic data would also weigh in.
"I see the (upward) trend continuing, but maybe the upside pace may level-off a little bit. I think we need some fresh indicators. The market doesn't go up in a straight line."
Equities rallied this week on the back of a raft of economic data which Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said boded well for interest rates.

Stals said this week that despite poor June credit extension data, up 16.39 percent from 16.65 percent in May, consumer inflation, money supply and trade balance data released earlier in the week held encouraging prospects for a cut in interest rates.

On Tuesday, data was released which showed annual inflation at a nine-month low of 8.8 percent in June and the country's trade balance at 4.15 billion rand in the same month from 1.75 billion rand in May.
Stals added, however, that it was impossible to be precise as to the timing when conditions would be right to ease monetary policy.

"All we can say is that hopefully in the second half of this year the situation will get easier on the financial side of the economy and it will be possible to relax on the monetary policy," he told Reuters on Thursday.
One equity trader said the fact that some market players' hopes of an immediate rate cut had not yet materialised could also dampen the market's enthusiasm next week.

"I think we were looking to the economic figures of this week to give us some direction but they did not add any positive news despite a very good CPI figure and a very good trade surplus figure," the dealer said.
"I think people looking for an interest rate cut thought these figures were sufficient to justify a cut now, literally in the next week or so," the dealer added.

Grahame Graham-Parker, a general manager at Infinity Asset Management was more optimistic about the market's prospects next week, saying he expected the market to rally on the back of a recovery in corporate earnings.
"I actually see the market continuing to rally," he told Reuters.
"You'll probably still see some underlying strength on the back of continued recovery in corporate earnings," he added.
Gold shares, which remain shrouded by bullion's woes could also lean on sentiment, dealers said.
"Gold is also a sentiment driver for our market and it's often the case that when bullion is down the rest of the market comes under a bit of pressure," an equity trader said.
The metal was trading at around $325 an ounce in London on Friday afternoon.

Among firms scheduled to report results in the coming week is Standard Bank Investment Corp (Stanbic) which is expected to post good half-year earnings on Tuesday despite debt loss of 230 million rand by insolvent local Pepsi bottler New Age Beverages.
There are no major economic indicators scheduled for release next week.
